title: Showing a Difference on the Line

steps.body: A difference has two honest drawings: walk backward from the bigger number, or mark both numbers and measure the gap between them.
steps.narration: A difference has two honest drawings: walk backward from the bigger number, or mark both numbers and measure the gap between them.

widget.prompt: Draw 57 − 23's tens as a walk: two backward ten-hops from 57.

commonLandings.feedback: A backward two — each drawn hop here is a full ten of the 23.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10, going backward. From 57, 2 hops land on 37.
widget.successFeedback: 37 — the tens are walked; three more backward ones would rest at 34.

options.label: Marks at 23 and 57; the gap between

predict.reveal: The distance from 23 up to 57 is the same 34 the backward walk finds — adding the marks would give 80, a total of two positions, not the gap between them.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2l show diff.
invariants: Position on the line IS the number: equal jumps cover equal amounts, and a journey's landing depends only on start, jump size, and direction for g2l show diff.
misconceptions: Treating marks as decoration — unequal spacing, jumps of the wrong size, or reading a start mark as a landing.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which change — start, jump size, or direction — would move the landing, and which would leave it alone?

explanationVariants: Gap or walk — both are honest.

widget.prompt: The drawing marks 33 and 53 and shades the gap between them. How long is that gap?

options.feedback: 86 adds the two marks together — the gap is the distance BETWEEN them, not their sum.
Correct — from 33 up to 53 is two ten-hops, so the shaded gap is 20 long.
That counts one ten-hop too many: 33 to 43 is one hop, 43 to 53 is the second — just 20.
19 comes from counting the marks between, not the hops — two ten-hops from 33 to 53 make 20 exactly.

steps.body: Complete the ones part of a subtraction route after the tens have already been drawn.

widget.prompt: After walking from 57 to 37 by tens, take three backward one-hops to land on 34.

commonLandings.feedback: That moves forward. The remaining three in 57 − 23 are backward one-hops.

widget.missFeedback: The tens route stops at 37; three backward one-hops finish at 34.
widget.successFeedback: 34 — the two ten-hops and three one-hops agree with 57 − 23.

widget.prompt: Which drawing shows the gap between 53 and 33?

options.label: Drawing A
options.feedback: Correct — the difference is the distance separating the two marks, hopped and counted.

options.label: Drawing B
options.feedback: Forward jumps grow the number; a difference either walks BACK or measures the gap.

options.label: Drawing C
options.feedback: That mark is the ANSWER, but a drawing of the difference must show where it came from.

options.label: Drawing D
options.feedback: Adding the endpoints measures no distance at all — the gap between them is the difference.
